key_insight: NereidVLA transfers marine visual and spatial knowledge into language-guided 3D underwater navigation. It first learns to understand underwater scenes without paired robot-motion data, then adapts that knowledge using expert trajectories.
problem_solved: Underwater robots must translate visual cues and language instructions into movement, but marine vision-language datasets rarely provide the paired robot trajectories needed for direct action training.
method: Train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relationships, and scene structure.
Learn this marine understanding without paired robot-motion supervision.
Adapt the pretrained model using expert trajectories for language-conditioned 3D navigation; the supplied abstract is truncated before further training details.
impact: The approach offers a way to use marine perception data when paired navigation demonstrations are scarce. It suggests a practical route from domain-specific scene understanding to robotic action, though the supplied excerpt includes no performance results.
visual_elements: Two-stage pipeline: marine examples → Sea2Know spatial understanding → expert-trajectory adaptation → NereidVLA navigation.

paper_title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
paper_authors: Chenjie Zhao, Zhiliang Zhu, Quan Chen, Yuquan Xue, Xingxue Shi
